references.note: Proof of Theorem 1, pp. 216-217, (1)-(4), the range k^(7/4) <= n < c k^2 / ln k: Ingham gives more than k^(3/4)/(c ln k) primes in (k/2, k/2 + k^(3/4)), so two of them are within c ln k of each other, and one of the two has two multiples in (n - k, n] and divides C(n,k).

literature_proposed.summary: This node is the upper range of Erdős-Lacampagne-Selfridge's Theorem 1: for k^(7/4) <= n with C n log2 k < k^2, some prime p in (k/2, k) divides C(n,k). Published 1993 and not formalised. The proof is Ingham's count of primes in (x, x + x^(3/4)) (deep, not in Mathlib), a pigeonhole to two close primes, and Kummer's theorem for the prime with two multiples in (n - k, n]; everything but Ingham is elementary. A translation could split off Ingham as its own hole, shared with erdos-1094--h3--h2--h2.
